newsitem.title: USA: Mobil forms global LPG coordination unit.
newsitem.headline: Mobil forms global LPG coordination unit.

text.p: Mobil Corp said it has formed a Global LPG Coordination unit with responsibilities for the coordination of the company's worldwide liquified petroleum gas business.

The company forecast "strong growth" in the worldwide market, which it valued at over $100 billion. LPG is the generic term for a mixture of propane and butane, typically handled as a liquid under pressure or refrigeration.
"This new unit will optimize LPG-related business opportunities that cross the company's independent upstream and downstream business units," said Lance Johnson.

"It will facilitate global product trading, waterborne transportation and marketing coordination to maximize the company's advantaged position in LPG," said Johnson, chief operating officer for Mobil's Supply Trading and Transportation business group.

"By fully integrating our expertise in production, product knowledge, marketing, logistics and transportation, we will be able to create business opportunities that would normally fall between the portfolios of our various business units," said Edgar "Tap" Taplin, who was named manager of the new organization.
Noting "inter-regional supply movements are expected to increase," he said this puts a premium on worldwide logistics capabilities and flexibility.
Mobil's base supply of LPG, which comes from equity production in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, exceeds 4.5 million metric tonnes per year, the company said.
It said additional production is projected from resources in Nigeria, Peru, Kazakstan and Qatar.
The company's worldwide sales and internal demand from its refineries and petrochemical plants currently exceed 7.5 million tonnes per year, over 4 percent of worldwide demand.
With worldwide LPG demand at 160-170 million tonnes per year, total end-user market value can exceed $100 billion per year.

Mobil said strong growth is forecast due in large part to its portability and clean environmental performance. Growth sectors include residential and commercial end-use in emerging markets. Its use as a petrochemical feed stock is also growing, where it is valued for its relatively high cracking yields. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
